title: Lactate Clearance Trend in Sepsis
scenario: A 55-year-old female client with suspected septic shock is started on IV fluid resuscitation and antibiotics. The nurse monitors serial lactate levels and hemodynamics over six hours.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Considering the six-hour trend, how should the nurse interpret the client's response to treatment?

options.text: The falling lactate with rising MAP and urine output indicates the resuscitation is effective
The client is deteriorating and needs escalation of care
The lactate trend is unrelated to perfusion status
The findings indicate the client is fluid overloaded

questions.rationale: Lactate clearing from 5.8 to 2.1 mmol/L alongside an improving MAP (58 to 74), slowing heart rate, and rising urine output shows restored tissue perfusion and an effective response to sepsis resuscitation.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Which findings in the trend support that tissue perfusion is improving? Select all that apply.

options.text: Lactate decreasing toward the normal range
Heart rate trending down toward normal

questions.rationale: A declining lactate, MAP above 65, increasing urine output, and a normalizing heart rate are all markers of restored perfusion. A persistently high lactate or falling urine output would indicate ongoing hypoperfusion.
